title: Game Design Theory
author: InformationTop5376
selftext:
So I’ve been working on my game for about three months now, and something I want to improve upon is my sense of good game design. I’ve been a gamer all my life so I do have some perspective from personal experience and what games were fun and what weren’t, but I know there is a whole lot more behind designing systems that work together so that the sum of their parts equate to a “good game”.

Would love recommendations for any timeless books on game design or ones that have helped you (particularly in the pre-AI days).

AI came up with a short list, but it’s AI so I’m taking the list with a grain of salt.

1 **A Theory of Fun** Understand why people play  
2 **The Art of Game Design** Learn to think like a game designer  
3 **Designing Games** Build satisfying interconnected systems  
4 **Game Design Workshop** Learn to prototype and validate ideas  
5 **Rules of Play** Develop a deeper theoretical foundation

Thanks!
